Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity planning — oversubscription question

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Our engineering team pushed back on one item we want to nail down before the SOW: Nebula is highly bursty during model training windows and occasional inference spikes. We need a clear policy for:

- How much transient (preemptible) capacity you would oversubscribe per reserved slab
- Priority and preemption order (which customers/queues trim first)
- Billing for ephemeral usage (amortized vs flat burst fees)

Attached is our current weekly spike profile and an initial estimate of requested peak qps. Could you propose a simple allocation approach we can include in the contract addendum?

Ari

Attachments: nebula_weekly_spike_profile.csv (attachment stub)
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity planning — oversubscription question

Ari —

Thanks for the clarity and the spike profile. I baked an initial proposal into the attached matrix (nebula_capacity_matrix_v3.xlsx) but high-level options below:

1) Fixed shoulder (recommended): reserve X GPUs for dedicated slab + a 20% ephemeral layer that is oversubscribed across the fleet. Ephemeral preemption is FIFO by queue age, with a soft SLO for 95th percentile latency.

2) Tiered preemption: partition ephemeral capacity into 3 priority bands (critical, standard, background). Nebula assigns workloads to bands; Redwood enforces preemption top-down.

3) Credit-based burst: customers buy burst credits that auto-consume when transient capacity used; credits are replenished monthly. We can also offer an amortized billing model if procurement prefers predictable cost.

Questions for your engineers — cc'ing Kar thik and Ben to confirm implementability:
- Do you have strict affinity constraints (e.g., certain models must run on pinned GPUs)?
- Expected average lifetime for bursts (seconds vs minutes)? That affects preemption granularity.

I'll schedule 30 minutes tomorrow to walk the options and show cost impact. If you want a draft SOW addendum after that, we can push a DocuSign link.

Best,
Grace

--
Grace O'Connor
Head of Sales, Dedicated Solutions
Redwood Inference

Grace / team —

Quick technical notes after reviewing Nebula's spike profile:

- Ephemeral slice sizing: 20% is reasonable for short bursts (median burst ~3 minutes) but if they see multi-hour training ramps we should size a separate ephemeral slab with eviction policies to avoid tail latency regressions.
- Preemption ordering: prefer queue-weighted preemption over pure FIFO. That gives us control to avoid starving long-running background batches. We can implement weights tied to priority bands in the policy engine.
- Affinity: if Ari's team needs GPU model affinity, we must mark those jobs as 'non-evictable' or run them on pinned reserved capacity. Non-evictable jobs would be excluded from the ephemeral pool.

Impacts on billing and SLOs: weighted preemption requires per-job metadata; that increases request footprint slightly but is standard. For billing, credit-based amortization is easiest for procurement (predictable).

I'll prototype a policy config snippet and a short ops runbook for how oncall will respond to preemption storms.

-Karthik

Grace / Karthik —

Thanks, this is helpful. A couple follow-ups from our infra side:

- Burst lifetime: mostly short (1–10 minutes) but during nightly retraining we can see sustained 2–4 hour windows.
- Affinity: yes — certain low-latency production models must stay on pinned capacity. Training and long batch jobs can use ephemeral.
- Procurement: credit model sounds workable; procurement prefers amortized costs rather than per-minute charges.

Can you show a sample cost table for: 10% / 20% / 30% ephemeral slices with both credit amortization and pay-as-you-go billing? Also please call out SLO rollback thresholds for eviction storms.

Ari
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai

Cc: ari.jenkins@nebulacorp.com
Date: 2026-10-11T10:55:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity planning — oversubscription question

Ari / Grace —

Attached is a quick cost sketch (we'll formalize in the SOW):

- 10% ephemeral: lowers unit cost impact but higher risk of headroom exhaustion during >1h training windows.
- 20% ephemeral: balanced — covers 95% of observed spikes in Nebula's profile and keeps 99th pct latency within target under normal conditions.
- 30% ephemeral: safest for spikes but ~15% higher monthly cost in amortized model.

SLO rollback thresholds (proposal):
- If eviction rate > 0.5% sustained for 30 minutes, trigger tiered rollback: reduce ephemeral to baseline, enable priority throttling, and open incident.
- If 95th pct latency increases >2x baseline for 15 minutes, initiate controlled fallbacks to compatible model variants.

I'll embed these numbers in the SOW addendum. Grace: do you want me to produce the DocuSign-ready PDF and the amortized pricing table?

-Ben
